cases.name: Cory Terlecky
cases.about: She was a server at the Mexican Village restaurant on 45th Street South in Fargo. Her obituary said, "After high school, Cory studied at both MState and MSUM Moorhead. She travelled to Mexico and Guatemala through MSUM for a student exchange program after which she was fluent in Spanish. Cory also travelled to London, Dubai, Portugal, Kenya and Germany. After she received her Associates Degree in Accounting, she worked for Vanity in Fargo. She also worked at restaurants in the area including at Petro, and was currently working as a server at Mexican Village. She enjoyed people, travelling, languages, and had a special interest in exploring different cultures. Cory was engaged to Ward Henderson. She loved her family and enjoyed going to family reunions."

cases.name: Ila Mae Lou Averson
cases.about: Her sister Carol Haak of Vergas, Minn. said she was a baseball fan and a fun-loving person. She built a 40-year career as a secretary for Northern States Power Co., and she was married for more than 50 years. la was born May 1, 1933, in Detroit Lakes, Minn., and grew up in Lake Park, Minn., where she graduated from high school.The Averson's had no children and were "very private people," Haak said. "They never really wanted anyone over there." Haak didn't know much about Louis. "My family hasn't had much to do with him," Haak said. But she'd talk with Ila every four to six weeks. "It was always Ila that called."

cases.name: Daisy Jade “Jupiter” Paulsen
cases.about: Her obituary, "Jupiter was a beautiful person filled with love and compassion for others. She was kind and strong willed and someone who never gave up. Jupiter was an artist who loved to paint and draw and a musician who played guitar and viola and loved to sing. She befriended the misfits as family and friends so they would know they were loved. Jupiter was the type of person to make flower crowns and give them to strangers just to see a smile. She cared and expressed love with her whole heart uplifting others in joy and happiness." She had just started a summer job at Arby’s.

cases.name: Isadora Wengel
cases.about: Please send information about her life, dreams or interests to shecounted@gmail.com
cases.narrative:
Investigators have reason to believe that dismemberment may have been involved in the disposal of her body. Over the course of the investigation, law enforcement searched the Fargo landfill 10 days in a row. Chief Zibolski did not share if anything of significance was found during those searches.

Fargo PD is calling for the public’s assistance in locating Isadora, directing focus to a black, 27-gallon, “fairly sizable” tote they believe could contain Isadora’s remains. Zibolski stated that two such totes were delivered to Hite’s apartment, but only one was recovered during the search of his apartment on January 9. Fargo PD is now asking residents of Fargo, Morehead City and Fergus Falls in North Dakota, Battle Lake and elsewhere in Otter Tail County, Minnesota, to search their properties “especially those in rural areas near roadways,” Zibolski said, “For any sign of this tote, or any sign of Isadora.”
